4. Mrs. Taposhi Rabeya, wife of absconding accused Faruk Thakur filed on 13-7-1995 Title Suit No. 143 of 1995 against Md Majibar Rahman and others for specific performance of a contract for sale of house No. 3A of Road No. 72of Gulshan Residential Area, ground floor which was let out to the victim Md Shamsul Alam, elder brother of the informant Nurul Alam and he used the same as his office-cum-godown of his business of contracts. On 16-7-95 learned Subordinate Judge passed an order of maintaining status quo in the suit property as regards alienation of the same in that suit. 

 7. Question before us is, whether petitioners who have been charged under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code are entitled to be enlarged on bail. It has already been noticed that petitioners were allowed bail by the learned Sessions Judge and learned Additional Sessions Judge after transfer of the case rejected their prayer for bail. It is true that there is no specific allegation against any of the petitioners of causing injury to the victim or any other person at the time of the occurrence. It is also true that the petitioners' name did not find place in the FIR. But there is no denial of the fact that petitioner Nos. 3-11 were arrested by the police on the date of occurrence from the place of occurrence thereabout or and there is clear allegation in the FIR that 20/25 persons had indiscriminately fired shots at the victim and his companions and at one stage victim was shot by absconding accused Faruk Thakur as a result of which he subsequently died in the hospital in the same night. In view of such allegations and arrest of the petitioner Nos. 3 to 11 from the spot and submission of charge-sheet against all of them after investigation non-mentioning of their name in the FIR has no bearing.It has already been noticed that absconding accused Faruk Thakur's wife Mrs. Tapasi Rabeya filed Title Suit No. 143 of 1995 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge Dhaka for specific performance of contract for sale of the disputed house No.3A of Road No. 72, Gulshan Residential-Area and had obtained an order for maintaining status quo regarding alienation of the suit property. There was no order of injunction restraining the house owner or the victim from entering into that property and there is no claim that from their side that in pursuance of an agreement for sale possession was delivered to the alleged buyer. We wonder how in a prestigious suburban Residential Area of the Capital city of Dhaka accused party could take forcible possession of that property by forming an unlawful assembly and in furtherance of such a common object cause death of the victim by gunshot injury. It appears from the addresses of the petitioner Nos. 3-11 that they hail from different areas of the country and are not permanent residents of Dhaka City. It was not possible on the part of the informant to know their identity at the time of the occurrence and it appears their identities were disclosed after their arrest. 

 11. Since the petitioners along with absconding accused have been charged under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code on the allegation of being armed members of an unlawful assembly and in furtherance of their common object of trespassing into the disputed house causing death to the victim by firearm shot, they are not entitled to bail under the provisions of section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the said offence is punishable with death or imprisonment for life.We have already seen that though the petitioners are not named in the First Information Report, most of them were arrested from the place of occurrence: Since petitioners were not granted bail by the learned Sessions Judge on merit and allowed bail on the assurance Of their senior lawyers that they would not misuse the privilege of bail in the facts and circumstances of the case as noticed above if is, not correct to say that they did not misuse the privilege of bail. Additional Sessions Judge has concurrent power as that of the Sessions Judge. As soon as a case is transferred from the Court of the Sessions Judge to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge the accused is required to pray, for fresh bail to the satisfaction of that Court as has been done by the petitioners. Additional Sessions Judge is not bound by the bail granted by the Sessions Judge. If he refuses bail to an accused who was earlier granted bail by the Sessions Judge that cannot be construed as cancellation of bail granted by the Sessions Judge. It is not that the Additional Sessions Judge did so in exercise of any revisional or appellate power but in exercise of concurrent power as he is to be satisfied as to the merit of granting bail to the accused. Since the refusal of the bail cannot be construed as cancellation there is no scope of giving any opportunity to the petitioners to show cause. Petitioners or for that matter the accused including the absconding accused could not produce before us anything to show that they had any right to enter into the disputed house or the house owner or his tenant victim was restrained by the civil Court from entering into that house. So, they cannot claim right to private defence. It is immaterial that the term of lease of the victim expired before the occurrence unless it could be shown that he was evicted by his lessor or he had voluntarily left the house. There is no charge of abetment but the charge is of being armed member of an unlawful assembly and in furtherance of their common object to murder the victim by one of them. So we find no merit in the contentions raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Since we have found that the petitioners are not entitled to bail we need not consider the propriety of the order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge refusing bail to the petitioners as we are not examining the legality of the order revision but considering the claim of the bail of the petitioners in exercise of power under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Learned Advocate for the petitioners relied on the decisions reported in 17 DLR (SC) 624, 35 DLR 167, 33 DLR 77, 40 DLR 507 and CrLJ 1981 page 229, in support of his contention that bail cannot be cancelled without giving the accused an opportunity to show cause and hearing. He also relied on the decisions reported in 11 BW (AD) 64 (1991), BCR 1987 (AD) 143, CrLJ 1982 page 2109 in support of his contentions that if there is no allegation of overt act against an accused charged with an offence under section 302 of the Penal Code his bail could not be cancelled. In support of his contention that bail cannot be cancelled or withheld as a measure of punishment learned Advocate relied on the decision reported in PLD1972(SC) 81.
